Verified the MaxLine claim empirically rather than accepting it: fold.go:43 caps canonical Data at MaxPayload (256KiB) and Type/Node/State at MaxShort (1KiB) each; marshalCanonical (types.go:345-363) only ever expands \u2028/\u2029/\ufffd 3 bytes to 6, so the worst-case line is about 515KiB against MaxLine of 1MiB. store_test.go:217-221 pins that Apply's payload cap fires first. The comment is accurate. The one envelope field Apply does not length-cap is Origin, but it is only ever set internally (builder.go:174) to a fixed-width LineHash, so there is no reachable gap.

Counted and MaxEvents() are not dead exports: machine/fork.go:300 and machine/fork.go:255 consume them for the in-memory fork check. TornFiles' "empty for the memory store" comment is true (store_mem.go:27-34 returns an empty slice after an existence check). Package coverage is 100% of statements (go tool cover over ./internal/fsm/run).

findings.note: TestQuotedDocumentationPathIsStillRecognizedAsProse does not pin the code path it is named for. Deleting the quoted-path branch of diffHeaderPath (taskdone.go:461-463, the ` "b/` LastIndex arm) leaves the entire internal/reviewers suite green: the test's fixture also carries a `+++ "b/docs/design notes.md"` header line, and postImagePath unquotes it there, so the diff --git decoder is never what makes the test pass. TestPathDecodersFailOpen:247 states the opposite in a comment ("the unquoted \" b/\" form, which the quoted branch does not cover"), implying the quoted branch is covered elsewhere. Statement coverage of diffHeaderPath reads 100%, which masks this. The behaviour itself is correct, so this is a test-strength gap, not a defect in shipped behaviour.

quoted-path arm of diffHeaderPath; deleting it fails no test in the package

findings.note: The seq-contiguity check in parseLines is not behaviourally asserted anywhere in the module. Deleting `if ev.Seq != seq { return CodeAuditChain "seq" }` (store.go:97-99) leaves ./internal/fsm/run, ./internal/fsm/machine and ./internal/fsm/record all green. The nearest test, store_test.go:403-411, is commented "seq gap in stored lines" but asserts only storeErr(err, CodeAuditChain) with no Seq and no Detail; with the seq check removed the rewritten line's hash makes the *next* line's prev check fail with the same code, so the assertion cannot tell the two apart. Statement coverage still shows parseLines at 100%. Functionally safe (Apply's ReasonSeqGap catches the same corruption downstream), but the check is unproven defence in depth.

evidence.note: chain seq check; removal breaks no test in run, machine or record
the seq-gap case asserts only the shared CodeAuditChain code, so the prev check satisfies it

findings.note: prepareCreate hardcodes DefaultMaxEvents instead of threading the store's configured cap. Mutating the argument to 0 breaks no test in ./internal/fsm/..., because TypeInit is not a countedType and the argument is never consulted on the Create path. Harmless today, but it silently diverges from Append (store_jsonl.go:231 passes s.opts.maxEvents()) and would ignore a caller's Options.MaxEvents the moment init becomes a counted type.

evidence.note: prepareAppend(nil, nil, FoldState{}, first, DefaultMaxEvents) ignores Options.MaxEvents

findings.note: Cross-shard observation, recorded here because this shard adds the fixture the row consumes. tests/go/test-fsm.sh:222 labels its row "injection: fenced values never appear raw in instructions", but the row's only assertion beyond exit statuses is that some llm_call event exists in audit.jsonl; the `call` binding is dead after the throw and nothing inspects `instructions` or searches for the planted payload. The suite passes (verified by running it), and the fencing property is genuinely covered at the Go level (internal/fsm/judge/judge_test.go:106-151, 733-734), so this is a mislabelled black-box row rather than a coverage hole. Separately, docs/specs/2026-08-27-metareview-0.9.0-fsm-cli.md:254-257 declares a black-box inventory of about 20 scenarios (sdlc-loop cumulative-convergence, no-findings, no-confirmed, dirty-tree, judge-swap-iter0, judge-swap-frozen, overflow-iterations, overflow-budget; review-loop adjudicate-fail, with-goldens, no-goldens, injection, torn; sdlc-loop-cmds cmd-guardrails, custom-outcome) and an "every outcome" row, while only five scenario directories exist on disk and the outcomes stalled, failed and custom are asserted nowhere in the script. Both belong to the test-fsm.sh and spec shards; flagged for the cross-shard pass.
